package_info.why_malicious: This package is part of a coordinated dependency confusion and namesquatting attack specifically targeting the Kraken cryptocurrency exchange. The package contains no legitimate source code and abuses npm's preinstall script to execute a shell command that collects host system information and exfiltrates it to an attacker-controlled domain. The intent is to impersonate a legitimate internal dependency, enabling supply chain compromise and reconnaissance of the victim environment.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During preinstall, the script executes a shell command that collects system information (output of uname -a, whoami, and hostname), sends this data via HTTP POST to https://www.analytics-google.com/collect, resulting in exfiltration of host and user details to an attacker-controlled server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The preinstall script executes a shell command that collects sensitive host and user information and immediately exfiltrates it to an external, attacker-controlled domain. This behavior is a clear indicator of malicious reconnaissance and is not consistent with any legitimate package installation process.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages rarely use preinstall scripts, and never to collect and transmit host or user data to untrusted, external domains. The absence of any actual package source code further violates expectations for a genuine dependency.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may collect telemetry or environment data, but only with explicit user consent and transmission to trusted, well-known domains. Such behavior is always disclosed and never hidden in a preinstall script.
key_indicators: preinstall script in package.json that executes shell commands
collection of system information (uname -a, whoami, hostname)
HTTP POST to hardcoded, attacker-controlled domain (www.analytics-google.com/collect)
absence of any legitimate source code or functionality in the package

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed as a result of dependency confusion or namesquatting, being mistaken for a legitimate internal dependency.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the preinstall script defined in package.json

attack_chain.action: The preinstall script executes, running a shell command to collect host system information (system details, username, hostname).
attack_chain.leads_to: Collected data is prepared for exfiltration

attack_chain.action: The collected host and user information is sent via HTTP POST to the attacker's domain (www.analytics-google.com/collect).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives reconnaissance data about the compromised environment

behavioral_signatures: npm preinstall script that executes shell commands making outbound network requests
collection and exfiltration of host and user information during package installation
npm packages with no source code except for a package.json containing suspicious scripts
file_indicators: package.json containing a preinstall script with curl or similar network utilities
absence of any .js, .ts, or other source files in the package directory (only package.json present)
network_indicators: HTTP POST requests to https://www.analytics-google.com/collect during npm install
Outbound network connections to untrusted or attacker-controlled domains initiated by npm scripts
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for preinstall scripts that invoke shell commands making network requests, especially those that collect and transmit system or user information to external domains. Flag packages that lack legitimate source code and contain only a package.json with suspicious scripts. Alert on outbound HTTP POST requests to known malicious or untrusted domains, such as www.analytics-google.com, during package installation.
